newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Woodside revenue jumps in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Woodside revenue jumps in first quarter.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said its sales revenue jumped to A$225.4 million in the first quarter of 1997 from A$156.8 million a year earlier.

Woodside's figures in its quarterly report to the Australian Stock Exchange showed the rise in sales revenue largely reflected a jump in liquids sales to A$99.7 million in the first quarter from A$44.3 million a year earlier.
Domestic gas and liquefied natural gas (LNG) sales also rose, to A$125.7 million in the quarter from A$112.5 million, Woodside said.

On the expenditure side, capital spending, including evaluation and development expenditure, jumped to A$36.3 million from A$8.9 million while exploration expenditure eased to A$9.8 million from A$11.27 milion, it said.
Woodside said revenue from condensate sales jumped to A$56.3 million in the first quarter from A$29.5 million a year earlier.
Revenue from crude oil rose to A$36.7 million from A$13.0 million and from liquefied petroleum gas to A$6.7 million from A$1.8 million.
Woodside has a 50 percent stake in the domestic gas phase of the North-West Shelf project offshore Western Australia and a one-sixth stake in the LNG and liquids phase.
